observation_summary: The Variance.evaluate method incorrectly processes the entire dataset instead of respecting the provided 'begin' and 'length' parameters, leading to incorrect statistical calculations.
reasoning_summary: The bug report explicitly states that the method ignores the 'length' parameter and processes the whole dataset. This is a procedural error in the implementation of the calculation method, where the logic fails to correctly constrain the data range as specified by the method signature. This fits the definition of Algorithm/Method as it is a local procedural logic error in how the data is iterated or accessed.
evidence_used: The method org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.moment.Variance.evaluate(double[] values, double[] weights, double mean, int begin, int length) does not work properly.
Looks like it ignores the length parameter and grabs the whole dataset.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the method fails to 'check' or respect the bounds, the root cause is the implementation of the calculation logic itself (the algorithm) which fails to use the provided parameters to slice the data correctly.
The interface signature is correct; the implementation simply fails to honor the contract defined by the parameters.
